chapter: Sansu, Irma, Lee Dorsey and the Meters
title: Sansu Enterprises and writing for Lee Dorsey
summary: With Marshall Sehorn he formed Sansu in 1965; Lee Dorsey's personality inspired songs like Working in the Coal Mine.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I don't think I've heard any tracks from that. Great. Great if you haven't. Something best left forgotten. Got some tape left on that. In 1965, if I'm not mistaken, we got together with Marshall Seahorn for Sansu Enterprises. And that's when you put out some great things about Lee Dorsey working in the coal mine. Holy Cow. Did those just come to you like driving in the car and things like that? Those are such, I think those kind of define the New Orleans fun song. Things that you always want to sing over and over again to yourself.

Lee Dorsey's way of being and his voice has a lot to do with those songs being in existence. None of the Lee Dorsey songs would have been written if it wasn't for Lee. I would say that. Well, in a way the same for Irma Thomas, but there are some songs that I wrote for Irma that sound quite normal to me as a normal song. But Lee Dorsey's songs were written where I wouldn't dare draw them on someone else.
